articles.title: Get a Perlegear Full Motion TV Wall Mount for Up to 90" TVs With 135lb Capacity for Just $33
articles.summary: The wall mount you choose is going to be supporting your expensive TV for years, so brand reliability is important. Perlegear is one of the biggest TV mount vendors on Amazon with plenty of reviews to back it up.
body: The Perlegear TV wall mount is rated for TVs 42" to 90" and up to 132 pounds. Of course to qualify for these ratings you'll need to screw the lag bolts into wood studs, concrete, brick, or any other strong surface; drywall will not suffice. Perlegear is no stranger to mounts, and its products include simple installation instructions that can be tackled as a relatively easy DIY project with only a few basic tools. The hardest part of the job is actually lifting your TV onto the mount.

Once installed, your TV is going to stay in place securely. The mount features thicker articulating arms and a larger reinforced wall plate than other brands at this price point. Security locks and anti-drop end caps are included so that there's no chance the TV will slide off the sides, even while you're positioning it. This is a full motion mount with tons of manueverability, including 20 degrees of tilt, 100 degrees of swivel, and 16.6" of extension. When folded all the way in, the TV extends only 3.3 inches from the wall.

articles.title: LEGO Venetian Neighborhood Set Is Coming in November
articles.summary: LEGO has announced a new 5,682-piece set called LEGO Icons Venetian Neighborhood. It’s an intricate set depicting several Italian buildings situated on a canal, with a bridge connecting them. It’s a well populated Venice scene, as it includes 17 minifigures.
body: It’s a lovely set that includes, according to the official description, a “luxury villa, an artisan glassblowing workshop and astronomical clock tower.” The buildings are built in a modular way that lets you remove roofs and entire floors to see the detailed interiors. In addition, the set can be separated into two distinct sections to create alternate display layouts, keeping things fresh.

Also included is a long gondola that fits neatly under the arched bridge. The 17 minifigures populating the neighborhood include gondoliers, musicians, tourists, and two carnival-goers dressed in costumes and masks. Also included is a 3D-printed street piano piece (you can see a close-up of it in the slideshow below).

Buying the set at the LEGO Store will also get you the LEGO Icons Venetian Water Taxi set (40898) as a free Gift With Purchase. It’s a 322-piece set containing a water taxi and a dock setting, plus captain and tourist minifigures, as well as two pigeon figures.

articles.title: 007 First Light On Switch 2 Includes Something No Other Platform Gets, And It’s Ridiculous
articles.summary: IO Interactive has announced the release date for 007 First Light's long-delayed Switch 2 version--March 18, 2027--and that's not all. People who preorder the game for Switch 2 are getting something no other platform has: a ridiculously oversized tie.
body: Not just any ridiculously oversized tie, however. People who preorder First Light for Switch 2 get the GoldenEye Suit, and it includes the suit and tie that Pierce Brosnan wore in the famous 1995 movie, including the oversized tie.
Brosnan wore a lot of suits in that movie, but the one being referenced here is the one with the oversized tie, which was the style at the time.

GoldenEye has a special history with Nintendo specifically, which may help explain why Switch 2 owners are getting this outfit and no one else is. After all, 1997's GoldenEye 007, which was based on the movie, is one of the most iconic N64 games of all time.
First Light has been a big hit, critically and commercially, scoring great reviews and selling more than 4 million copies, and that's before the Switch 2 version even comes out.

articles.title: A Massive Decompilation Community Is Shutting Down, Thanks to the Deluge of AI Decomps and Ports
articles.summary: If you've been on gaming Twitter at all over the last month, you're probably aware of the massive wave of people using AI to rapidly decompile, port, and remix games. That wave of AI decomps has forced a massive decompilation community to sunset.
body: In a blog post, admin @encounter from decomp.dev, a community repository for people to track decompilation posts, cites a wave of bad actors who are using AI to essentially steal the hard work of programmers working on existing decompilation projects.

The act of decompiling games itself isn't new, and people have been taking games and trying to decompile them down to the source code for years. But what was once a herculean task requiring coding expertise can now be done with little effort thanks to new AI models like GPT 6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5.

The blog post doesn't blame the models themselves for the surge of vibe-coded decompilations and ports, but rather claims that bad actors are taking existing projects and then using AI to rush them to completion. While there might be some developers who are open to people with a Claude subscription using their work to create, say, a browser port of Halo, that should be up to each developer.

articles.title: GTA 6 Isn’t Showing Boobie In Promotional Material
articles.summary: The marketing machine for Grand Theft Auto 6 is at full steam, and while Rockstar Games is showcasing many of the characters players will be encountering in the open-world crime game, one character with a very distinct name has been largely absent from promos.
body: Viewers of the GTA 6 Extended Look might have been snickering every time protagonists Jason and Lucia uttered the word "Boobie," but the official GTA 6 website indicates that the character of Boobie Ike is a Vice City powerhouse. Though he's implied to be a highly influential figure in the game's story, he hasn't made an appearance in any trailers.

Boobie is the owner of the Jack of Hearts club, seen in the extended look trailer. His "legitimate empire" also includes real estate investments and a recording studio, and in his words, "the drug money pay for it all." The first segment of the extended look video has Jason and Lucia making a pickup on behalf of Boobie, and simply saying his name was enough to grant them access.

The lack of Boobie in any GTA 6 trailers does prompt curiosity about his larger role in the story. It has already been the subject of speculation in social media posts and YouTube videos, with some predicting that he'll turn out to be an antagonist who double-crosses Jason and Lucia. It's also possible that Boobie's presence in the story will be by name only, as he pulls strings from the background.

articles.title: We’re Getting A WWE And Street Fighter Crossover, And It’s Pretty Weird
articles.summary: Ahead of the Street Fighter movie 's release this week, 2K Games has announced a new DLC pack for WWE 2K26 that lets you dress several WWE performers as Street Fighter action figures.
body: You can make the likes of Rey Mysterio and The Rock look like oversized toys, and each version of the WWE star will also come equipped with Street Fighter-inspired moves like the Shinku Hadoken, Psycho Crusher, Spiral Arrow, Electric Thunder, and Shoryuken. Pricing hasn't been revealed yet, but generally, these character packs cost around $15.

Strangely, there's no Cody Rhodes Street Fighter skin, which is kind of weird since he plays Guile in the movie and has even cosplayed as him at WWE live events. Additionally, the pack includes 15 Create-a-Superstar parts from several other Street Fighter characters: Akuma, Vega, and Chun-Li. Each Street Fighter skin is inspired by the Mattel Elite Collection WWE X Street Fighter figures, so this is merchandising taken to a new extreme. To paraphrase Danhausen, these are cursed.

Reviews have also begun appearing online for Street Fighter, and on GameSpot's sister site Metacritic, the film has a "mixed or average" metascore of 46 from 19 reviews. Critics say that the movie's story is an absolute mess, and it's barely held together by several stylish fight scenes across its two-hour runtime.

articles.title: Sega Pulls Total War: Shogun 2 Remaster After Backlash Over AI-Upscaled Graphics
articles.summary: Following player backlash, Sega and Creative Assembly have yanked Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition from sale and have replaced it with the original 2011 version.
body: "We're aware that Total War: Shogun 2 - Complete Edition has fallen short of both your expectations and our own standards," Sega wrote in a statement that did not address the AI criticisms at all. "We've seen your feedback, comments, and reviews. We agree that the current experience is not where it needs to be."

Fans have also taken to social media to show off legacy bugs that still haven't been addressed in this new edition, and Sega said that it's "working closely" with its "development partners" to identify and address these issues. Unsurprisingly, the game has an overwhelmingly negative rating on Steam currently, with over 81% of players urging people to give it a skip.

"Horrific graphical bug makes the vegetation in battle map terrible to look at. There's no way to disable the vegetation," one oddly specific player review reads," amongst hundreds of other negative pieces of feedback.

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave gets its first wave of DLC today, and an expansion pass to include it
articles.summary: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems have released an expansion pass for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, introducing a string of DLC additions to the tactical RPG starting today, and through into 2027.
body: The expansion pass, which can be bought on the Nintendo eShop for $34.99 / £29.99, comes in three parts. For those who buy it now, a selection of weapons are made available to use within the game. The second part of the expansion pass arrives this holiday season, and the final part arrives in 2027.
We already know a bit about what's coming in these latter DLC releases. The second portion features additional outfits for the game's cast, alongside three new allies: Aurora, Smyrnos, and Jurah.

The final segment of the pass looks to be the most substantial; introducing new stories to play, new allies, classes, and additional goodies. Those new stories make an already chunky game even larger, something that should give people a reason to go back to the RPG next year, and those yet to pick up the game, a convenient jumping-on point.

Fortune's Weave has been met with critical acclaim and sizable early sales figures. In Eurogamer's review, the game is described as "a synergy of everything that has made the series great for generations", and "a sumptuous feast of a game".
points: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems have released an expansion pass for Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, introducing a string of DLC additions to the tactical RPG starting today, and through into 2027.

body: Larian Studios’ Divinity: Original Sin 2, a sprawling fantasy RPG about a party of Source-wielding outcasts, lets you or play as the Red Prince. He’s an exiled lizard crown prince who thinks he’s better than you. articles.title: Control Resonant sells 1 million copies in 3 weeks to become Remedy's fastest-selling game ever
articles.summary: Remedy announced today that Control Resonant has surpassed one million copies sold, moving past Alan Wake 2 to become "the fastest-selling game in Remedy Entertainment's 31-year history." Thank you for the support ❤️ For playing, sharing, and being a part of the community.#CONTROLResonant.
body: Three weeks to a million copies isn't exactly a blistering pace by conventional videogame standards: The Blood of Dawnwalker hit the mark in three days, Wardogs did it in one, and Subnautica 2 put out twice that number in just 12 hours.

But despite producing a string of unique, memorable, and critically acclaimed games, Remedy has never really smashed a massive home run in the sales department. Even Alan Wake 2, which won numerous awards for narrative and art direction in 2023 (and would have claimed so many more if not for the Baldur's Gate 3 behemoth) took two months to sell a million copies, significantly outpacing the original Control and making it the studio's fastest-selling game at that time.

Remedy's more pressing problem, though, is profit: It took more than a year, and two million copies sold, before Alan Wake 2 actually started making money for Remedy. Addressing that shortcoming was the top priority for Jean-Charles Gaudechon, who took over as the company's new CEO in February: Remedy chairman Henri Österlund said at the time that Gaudechon's appointment was intended "to lead Remedy into a phase of profitable growth."

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont's Curse review - inspired by great ideas, but doomed by questionable execution
articles.summary: In my office, I have a collage of Ordnance Survey maps plastered across my wall. They're from places I've lived - Derbyshire, East London, Bournemouth, Bristol - with cycle routes, country roads, and parks highlighted and circled.
body: Perhaps that's why I love Metroidvanias so much. Really, the game is the map. Is there anything more intoxicating than pushing your palms up against the walls supposedly keeping you in and knowing that - somewhere - there's a hidden path leading to the other side? Over the years, you develop an instinct for it; you get to play against the sadistic engineers of these labyrinthine spaces. 'I see your mysterious overhang,' you say, 'and jump through your roof. I see your egregious slab of a wall, and phase through its illusion.'

And Castlevania: Belmont's Curse has all this in spades. There are so many sly nuances tucked away around the streets of Paris and within Dracula's Castle that it's like I'm instantly transported back to my pre-pubescent self, nudging the D-Pad against every wall in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night in a belligerent attempt to sniff out its secrets.
